title: Cost bound for one-way communication complexity
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function and let $n \in \bbn$. The one-way deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n$ if and only if there exists a one-way deterministic protocol $p$ that computes $f$ and whose bit cost satisfies $\mathrm{cost}(p) \le n$.
hypotheses_covered: ≤ n comparison in the extended naturals ℕ∞
existence of a protocol computing f with cost ≤ n
replaced:
For a function $f$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the one-way complexity of $f$ is at most $n$
if and only if there exists a one-way protocol $p$ that computes $f$ with
$p.\mathtt{cost} \le n$.
